```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "R code for the setup: every number on this page is read here"
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(knitr))
for (f in list.files("../R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
# The explorer's own data file, read as the explorer reads it (R/site.R)
G <- read_site_grid_js("explorer/grid.js")
hl <- read.csv("data/headlines.csv")
printed <- read.csv("data/printed-tables.csv")
h <- function(v, q, col = "reproduced") hl[[col]][hl$version == v & hl$quantity == q]
ss <- formals(compute_npv_mc_ssrn)
num <- function(x, d = 1, plus = FALSE) {
  s <- formatC(abs(x), format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
  ifelse(x < 0, paste0("−", s), if (plus) paste0("+", s) else s)
}
words <- function(n) c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")[n]
dollars <- function(x) gsub("$", "\\$", x, fixed = TRUE)   # a literal $ in a markdown table cell
md_table <- function(d) {
  d[] <- lapply(d, dollars)
  cat("\n\n::: {.table-scroll}\n\n", paste(kable(d, format = "pipe", align = "l"), collapse = "\n"),
      "\n\n:::\n\n", sep = "")
}
main <- site_grid_js_cell(G, from = "nber")[["mean_npv"]]
seeded <- h("nber", "mc_mean_npv")
# the first version's Monte Carlo: the explorer's "ssrn" setting
first <- site_grid_js_cell(G, from = "ssrn")[["mean_npv"]]
# the first version's Table 9, recomputed (the explorer cannot fix the revenue at one value)
t9 <- compute_npv_table9()
p9 <- printed[printed$table == "table9" & printed$column == "npv", ]
t9$printed <- p9$printed[match(paste0(t9$scenario, "@", t9$r), p9$row)]
# the repository's 2% case (NPV_plots/npv_decomposition_2pct.pdf prints -67.2): no OPA setting;
# hand-built inputs so that f = 1 - WT/baseline equals the script's 0.554 (as in
# feedback/scenario-tests-2026-10-15/jr-sensitivity.R, case 5)
base2 <- 0.02 * ss$baseline_revenue / 0.05
two_pct <- compute_npv_table9(baseline = base2,
  scenarios = list(two_pct = list(label = "2%", WT = (1 - 0.554) * base2, C = 4.55)), r_values = 0.03)$npv
match_word <- function(printed, ...) if (any(round(c(...), 1) == printed)) "Match" else "No match"
nine <- list(six_confirmed = "Six departures", central = "Central", lit_calibrated = "Literature calibrated")
rows9 <- lapply(names(nine), function(s) {
  x <- t9[t9$scenario == s, ]
  x <- x[order(x$r), ]
  data.frame(
    Variation = sprintf("%s: revenue $%sB, income tax $%sB a year, share lost %s%%", nine[[s]],
                        sub("0$", "", formatC(x$WT[1], format = "f", digits = 2)),
                        sub("0$", "", formatC(x$C[1], format = "f", digits = 2)), num(100 * x$f[1], 1)),
    Source = "SSRN, Table 9",
    Printed = paste(num(x$printed, 1, plus = TRUE), collapse = " / "),
    `This OPA` = paste(num(x$npv, 2, plus = TRUE), collapse = " / "),
    Result = if (all(round(x$npv, 1) == x$printed)) "Match" else "No match",
    `How to set it` = "R code", check.names = FALSE)
})
dl <- function(k, i) G$dials[[which(vapply(G$dials, `[[`, "", "key") == k)]]$labels[[i + 1L]]
sl <- unlist(G$named$ssrn); names(sl) <- vapply(G$dials, `[[`, "", "key")
results <- rbind(
  data.frame(Variation = "Main assumptions, for reference", Source = "NBER, p.35",
             Printed = num(h("nber", "mc_mean_npv", "printed"), 1),
             `This OPA` = sprintf("%s (seeded run %s)", num(main, 2), num(seeded, 2)),
             Result = match_word(h("nber", "mc_mean_npv", "printed"), main, seeded),
             `How to set it` = "Explorer, as it opens", check.names = FALSE),
  data.frame(Variation = sprintf("Revenue drawn from $%sB to $%sB, and the share lost tied to the revenue (f = 1 − revenue / %s)",
                                 dl("wt_lo", sl[["wt_lo"]]), dl("wt_hi", sl[["wt_hi"]]), ss$baseline_revenue),
             Source = "SSRN, p.20", Printed = num(h("ssrn", "mc_mean_npv", "printed"), 1),
             `This OPA` = num(first, 2), Result = match_word(h("ssrn", "mc_mean_npv", "printed"), first),
             `How to set it` = sprintf("Explorer: from the main setting, set the lowest revenue to %s, the highest to %s and the share lost to \"%s\"",
                                       dl("wt_lo", sl[["wt_lo"]]), dl("wt_hi", sl[["wt_hi"]]), dl("f", sl[["f"]])),
             check.names = FALSE),
  do.call(rbind, rows9),
  data.frame(Variation = "Tax rate 2% instead of 5%, central inputs, r − g of 3%",
             Source = "Authors' repository, a plot", Printed = num(-67.2, 1), `This OPA` = "none",
             Result = "Cannot be set", `How to set it` = "None", check.names = FALSE))
n_printed <- nrow(results) - 2                  # the variations the papers print
n_match <- sum(results$Result[2:(n_printed + 1)] == "Match")
settings <- site_checks_table(G)
```

All `r words(n_printed)` variations the JR papers print `r if (n_match == n_printed) "reproduce" else paste0("are checked; ", words(n_match), " reproduce")` at the paper's rounding. A fifth, in the
authors' repository, uses a lower tax rate, which cannot be set in this OPA. None of the five
changes a single assumption, so the papers give no printed check of the explorer's named
settings.

## What was checked

The main estimate of the JR analysis is a mean net present value of [−$38.9 billion]{style="white-space:nowrap"} (NBER chapter,
September 2026, p.35). This OPA computes it as [−$`r num(abs(main), 2)` billion]{style="white-space:nowrap"} exactly, and as [−$`r num(abs(seeded), 2)` billion]{style="white-space:nowrap"}
with the authors' random seed. The September chapter prints no net present value under other
assumptions. The first version (SSRN, March 2026) prints four, and the authors' public repository
holds one more. Each check below sets the same assumptions in this OPA and compares the result
with the printed figure.

Each of the five changes two or more inputs at once from the main estimate. The first version's
Monte Carlo changes the revenue range and the rule for the share of income tax lost. Each
scenario of its Table 9 fixes four inputs at single values.

## Results

All figures are net present values in billions of dollars. Table 9 prints three values per
scenario, one for each value of r − g (`r r9 <- paste0(100 * sort(unique(t9$r)), "%"); paste(paste(head(r9, -1), collapse = ", "), "and", tail(r9, 1))`). "Match" means this OPA's value rounds to
the printed figure.

```{r}
#| label: results
#| results: asis
#| code-summary: "R code for the results table"
md_table(results)
```

## What could not be checked

**The tax rate.** This OPA has no setting for a wealth tax rate other than 5%. The repository's 2%
case is reproduced only by building its inputs by hand (`r num(two_pct, 2)`).

**The explorer's named settings.** The explorer offers "Rate 1.5%" and "Rate 4.5%", each of
which changes one input from the main estimate, and "Litigation weight q = 0.5", which changes two
(q, and the revenue floor raised to 35 so the risk is not counted twice). The authors print no net
present value for any of them.

## Who ran these checks

Claude Code agents chose the variations from the papers and ran the checks on 15 October 2026.
The scripts were then rerun once, in a separate session, with the same results. The author has
not yet reviewed these checks.

To rerun them from the repository root, with a clone of the authors' repository:

```sh
export RAUH_REPO_DIR=<path to the authors' repository>
Rscript feedback/scenario-tests-2026-10-15/jr-sensitivity.R
```

The full record, with the source of every figure, is in
[jr-sensitivity.md](https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40/blob/main/feedback/scenario-tests-2026-10-15/jr-sensitivity.md).
A second record, [jr.md](https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40/blob/main/feedback/scenario-tests-2026-10-15/jr.md),
checks ten other numbers the papers print. Seven match and two are close (mismatches 4, 6 and 9,
and a semi-elasticity of 5.73 against 5.72 from the chapter's own inputs). The chapter's "expanded
departures" (Table 8, about 42% of the base) matches no grouping of the authors' departure
records.

## Settings the papers do not print

This OPA lets a reader change assumptions the papers hold fixed. The table below lists
`r words(nrow(settings) - 1)` such changes, each made from the September chapter's main
assumptions, with the result this OPA gives. Each changes one assumption, except the litigation
weight, which the explorer pairs with a higher revenue floor. The papers print no figure for any of
them, so they are untested against the authors' own work.

We have sent this table to the original authors, requesting them to test whether they obtain the
same results. We will update the responses here.

The mean net present value is in billions of dollars. This OPA computes the exact average of the
authors' formula over the same random draws, not a new seeded run. A seeded run of the authors'
script differs from it by sampling error only (at the main setting, `r num(seeded, 2)` against `r num(main, 2)`). Each setting can be made
in the [explorer](explorer/), and each value below is the one the explorer shows.

```{r}
#| label: settings
#| results: asis
#| code-summary: "R code for the settings table, read from the explorer's grid.js"
md_table(data.frame(
  `Setting changed from the main assumptions` = settings$setting,
  `Mean net present value` = num(settings$mean_npv, 2),
  `Share of runs below zero` = paste0(num(settings$pct_negative, 1), "%"),
  `Authors' result` = c("", rep("Pending", nrow(settings) - 1)),
  check.names = FALSE))
```

The litigation row raises the lowest revenue with q, as the explorer's "`r G$named_labels$q50`"
setting does. The draw's 0 floor already halves the mean revenue (0.5 × `r formals(compute_npv_mc_nber)$wt_max`), so q with that
floor would count the risk of the Act being struck down twice.

The share of runs below zero is exact (`r num(settings$pct_negative[1], 1)`%). The authors' seeded run gives
`r num(h("nber", "mc_pct_negative"), 2)`%, printed `r h("nber", "mc_pct_negative", "printed")`%.

The two tables are built when this page is rendered: the settings from the explorer's data file,
`site/explorer/grid.js`, and the variations from the same pipeline, so they cannot drift from the
explorer. `tests/testthat/test-site.R` checks the rendered page against that file.
